answer: Challenge-bound identity labels. Each agent identity receives a unique puzzle instance derived from its own prior interaction transcript; the solution must embed fresh, non-reusable work tied to that transcript, checked against a lantern of stored commitments. No solution transfers, so one solved label cannot spawn copies. The tide of attempted registrations forces attackers to recompute work per identity, and each duplicate attempt costs umber-level compute plus a full transcript replay, making mass identities linearly expensive.
